assessments.reasoning: The original at https://www.latex-project.org/lppl/lppl-1-3c.txt identifies “LPPL Version 1.3c  2008-05-04” and “Copyright 1999 2002-2008 LaTeX3 Project.” Capture 576612b9a1ef41b6a75eb06379bbfada at 2026-11-28T11:15:06Z returned HTTP 200 and one UTF-8 body from the title through the final “   the Work.\n\n”. Its single range [0,19036) and whole-file receipt both report SHA-256 c1ae6e179a6d28bbd5c483fbacc744acc75e922d598281dc3390aab26126e163. The publisher, edition and copyright establish the authority for the header. The length, digest and edition-specific body distinguish this capture from 1.3a despite their identical grant and closing line.

challenge.method: Checked the 1.3c original independently for edition substitution, a narrower copyright grant, and carve-outs in the component exemptions, model-license guidance and section on nonreplacement derived works. Compared the sample notice’s version election with its separate statement about LaTeX distributions.
challenge.results: The nonreplacement provision disapplies clauses 6b and 6d for specified Derived Works. Clause 6 component exemptions likewise govern the Work. Neither qualifies the document header. The example uses “Copyright 2008 M. Y. Name” and offers version 1.3 or later. Its separate reference to 1.3c or later describes inclusion in LaTeX distributions from 2008 onward. The instructions to put a holder’s name, year and licensing statement in each component address authors applying LPPL to their own works. The permission to use LPPL as a model concerns a separately identified license.

limitations: The finding covers the specified 1.3c file. The example supplies no version election, copyright attribution, maintainer appointment or file inventory for an actual project.
The digest comparison uses this review’s acquisition receipt. The prescribed calls did not include a separate local hash calculation or verification of the earlier research capture.
reasoning: Lines 7–8 of LPPL 1.3c grant everyone permission to distribute verbatim copies of the license document and expressly prohibit modifying it. The complete identified plaintext falls within the grant, including the existing notices, the illustrative project notice and the edition’s discussion of nonreplacement derived works.
